Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Here’s a simple starting map:
Whiskey — warm, rich, and often oaky; Bourbon tends toward vanilla/caramel, Rye is spicier, and Scotch can range from fruity to smoky.
Tequila — made from agave; bright and earthy. Blanco is fresh and crisp, while aged styles are smoother and more vanilla-like.
Rum — often easygoing and slightly sweet; white rum suits refreshing cocktails, while aged rum is richer and more sippable.
Gin — botanical and aromatic, usually led by juniper; great if you enjoy herbal or citrusy flavors.
Vodka — clean and neutral; an easy base for cocktails when you don’t want a strong spirit flavor.
Brandy — fruit-based and smooth, often with dried-fruit and oak notes.
Flaviar carries whiskey, rum, gin, tequila, vodka, brandy, and more, from familiar classics to craft and rare bottles.  For a first tasting, comparing a few spirits from the same family can make the differences easier to notice. 
Do you usually prefer sweet, smoky, spicy, fresh, or herbal flavors?
